title: Quantum-Enhanced Synthetic Data Generation Using Quantum Circuit Born Machines for Imbalanced Tabular Learning
authors: Tanapol Nuatho, Narisorn Sangnakara, Prapong Prechaprapranwong, Rajchawit Sarochawikasit
abstract: Data scarcity and class imbalance are persistent challenges in machine learning that degrade model generalization and introduce predictive bias. We present a hybrid quantum-classical framework for synthetic data generation using a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) to address these limitations. The proposed approach exploits quantum mechanical properties -- superposition and entanglement -- within a parameterized variational quantum circuit to model complex probability distributions that are difficult for classical generative methods to capture. Experiments are conducted on two tabular benchmark datasets: the Iris dataset and the Telco Customer Churn dataset. Preprocessing includes normalization and PCA-based dimensionality reduction to enable efficient basis encoding for quantum circuits. The QCBM is trained by minimizing Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between real and generated data distributions using a gradient-based parameter-shift optimization rule. Augmenting training data with QCBM-generated synthetic samples at 40-50% of the minority class improves F1-score by approximately 5-15% and minority-class recall by 10-25%. Cross-domain evaluations (Train on Synthetic, Test on Real; and Train on Real, Test on Synthetic) reveal a performance gap of only 3-10%, indicating strong distributional fidelity. Comparative analysis against classical oversampling methods -- SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, KMeansSMOTE, and SVM-SMOTE -- shows that QCBM achieves competitive classification performance and produces lower Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) on the Telco dataset, suggesting superior structural similarity in certain imbalanced settings. These findings establish QCBM as a viable complementary tool for data augmentation, particularly for low-dimensional structured tabular data with class imbalance.
summary: This work proposes using a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) within a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline to generate synthetic data for imbalanced tabular datasets. By leveraging quantum properties like entanglement, the QCBM achieves superior structural similarity compared to classical oversampling methods. This augmentation significantly boosts downstream classification performance on real-world benchmarks.
main_problem: The paper addresses data scarcity and class imbalance, common challenges in machine learning that degrade model generalization.
main_result: Using a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) for synthetic data augmentation improves classification metrics like F1-score by 5–15% on structured tabular datasets.
method: A hybrid quantum-classical framework is employed where the QCBM models complex probability distributions to generate synthetic samples, which are then used to augment imbalanced training data.
model_or_system: The core model is the Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM), which utilizes a parameterized variational quantum circuit $U(\theta)$ exploiting superposition and entanglement. The process involves encoding classical data into quantum states for distribution modeling.
key_observables: Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), F1-score, and minority-class recall are used to quantify distribution fidelity and classification performance.
important_parameters: The synthetic data augmentation ratio (tested at 30–50% of the minority class), circuit depth ($L$), and optimization parameters ($	heta$) are key variables.
main_assumptions: Assumptions include the tractability of basis encoding via PCA dimensionality reduction for near-term quantum simulators, and that the QCBM can capture complex cross-feature correlations better than classical methods like SMOTE.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables comparing KL Divergence and MMD across datasets (Iris/Telco) and performance metrics (F1, AUC-ROC) for various oversampling techniques.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the QCBM framework (preprocessing via PCA, training by minimizing KL divergence using parameter-shift rule), evaluates its efficacy through data augmentation protocols (DA, TSTR, TRTS), and compares results against established classical baselines.
why_interesting: While focused on ML, the paper's reliance on variational quantum circuits to model complex probability distributions touches upon quantum state tomography and characterizing quantum process fidelity, which are relevant areas in quantum information theory.
